definitions.explanation: An imaginary horizontal line on the earth's surface, running east-west, marking degrees of latitude from the equator.

examples.japanese: {地図|ちず}に{緯線|いせん}を{引|ひ}く。
examples.english: To draw lines of latitude on a map.

examples.japanese: {赤道|せきどう}は{緯度|いど}ゼロ{度|ど}の{緯線|いせん}である。
examples.english: The equator is the line of latitude at zero degrees.

examples.japanese: {北緯|ほくい}38{度|ど}の{緯線|いせん}は{朝鮮半島|ちょうせんはんとう}の{軍事境界線|ぐんじきょうかいせん}の{目安|めやす}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The 38th parallel north is known as a rough marker for the military demarcation line on the Korean Peninsula.

notes:
A geography term composed of {緯|い} (latitude) and {線|せん} (line). Lines of latitude run horizontally (east-west) around the globe, in contrast to {経線|けいせん} (lines of longitude), which run vertically (north-south).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緯線|いせん}と{経線|けいせん} — latitude and longitude lines
- {北緯|ほくい}〜{度|ど}の{緯線|いせん} — the latitude line at 〜 degrees north
- {緯線|いせん}に{沿|そ}って — along the line of latitude

RELATED WORDS:
- {経線|けいせん} — line of longitude; meridian
- {緯度|いど} — latitude (the measurement itself)
- {赤道|せきどう} — equator (the zero-degree latitude line)
